text:
maya: PD page: service=edge-router triggered — high 5xx rate (503/504) immediately after edge rollout. seeing ~12% 5xx across eu-west. tagging oncall. pls ack.
pd-bot: PagerDuty: INCIDENT #PD12345 -> edge-router | Trigger: 5xx-rate > 10% | Severity: high | https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345
oncall-bot: @maya thanks — paging primary oncall: @sam
sam: acked. jumping on it. can someone paste the release id?
maya: rollout id: rollout-2026-03-14-edge-v2. Traffic shift started at 22:14 UTC. Canary weight 20% -> 100% over ~6m.
li: logs look noisy — a backend service (edge-auth) returning 502/503 for requests routed to new image. stack traces show upstream 502s from auth-proxy.
nina: adding telemetry: kinesis spike + kv cache miss rate doubled. could be a connection pool exhaustion. cpu for the edge pods is fine.
sam: ok running quick `kubectl get pods -n edge -l rollout=rollout-2026-03-14 -o wide` to confirm.

sam: pod list shows new image on node group-5, restart count is low. but readiness probes are flapping on 6/8 pods.
maya: repro curl to edge host returns 503 with body: "temporary unavailable" — correlation id present.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: rollout-2026-03-14 completed canary -> primary. Image: ghcr.io/redwood/edge:2026-03-14-v2
pd-bot: Escalation: If not acknowledged in 5m, will notify secondary oncall.
sam: i'm going to pause traffic to the new rollout if we can. Nina, can you open a quick canary diversion?
nina: starting traffic diversion: route 80% back to stable (edge:v1) via traffic-manager policy. applying now.

nina: `kubectl patch svc edge-router -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"rollout":"stable"}}}'` applied (pseudo). traffic shift in progress.
maya: customer impact — error rate for API calls in eu-west jumped to 11.8% p99 latency up 300ms. preliminary subset of customers (api keys starting with prod-*) effected. support tickets inbound.
sam: good. after diversion error rate falling to 2.1% in the last 60s. keep monitoring.

li: digging into auth-proxy logs: `ERROR connection refused` to upstream auth-db on node group-5. connection pool exhausted after spike in new code path.
li: stack diff points to new header propagation from v2 causing extra auth calls per request.
maya: sounds like a functional regression in v2. recommend rollback to v1 if we see sustained errors.

sam: agreed. preparing rollback. rolling rollback to image edge:v1 for rollout-2026-03-14. executing now.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated -> rollout-2026-03-14 -> target image: ghcr.io/redwood/edge:2026-03-07-v1

sam: rollback is progressing; pods on node group-5 terminating, stable pods scaling up.
nina: traffic is now 100% stable edge:v1. metrics: 5xx down to baseline 0.6% in eu-west.
maya: filing incident ticket and customer impact note. summarizing: deploy v2 caused auth-proxy to increase upstream calls, exhausted pools causing 503s. immediate mitigation: traffic diversion -> rollback. ETA for RCA: 48h.

pd-bot: Incident PD12345 acknowledged by sam. Status: mitigated. Closing will require RCA doc link.

sam: leaving notes for handoff to morning oncall @li for RCA triage. @maya please add support ticket list to incident timeline.

maya: added support ticket IDs: #SUP-9082, #SUP-9083, #SUP-9087. Notifying affected customers via status page draft.

li: will start replaying auth call traces and reproduce locally. initial suspicion: header duplication causing double auth lookups.
nina: follow-up: add circuit breaker and connection pool guard to auth-proxy in short term. open PR for abort-on-flood.

sam: thanks everyone. closing handoff — oncall remains aware. if PD auto-escalates reopen channel.

maya: :thumbsup: good mitigation. please include exact rollout timestamps in RCA.

pd-bot: PD12345 -> status: resolved (mitigated). timeline recorded.

oncall-bot: Handoff: primary sam -> li for RCA/next steps. Channel archived for timeline extraction.

maya: last note — we should add a preflight that checks for additional auth calls in canary before full rollout. documented in postmortem action items.
